Private Montezuma Castle Tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale

Scottsdale Sprinters runs a private Montezuma Castle tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale as one vehicle and one chauffeur held for a 7-hour day: the group is driven to the confirmed monument stop, waited on while you walk the trail, and driven home. The question to settle first is what a visit actually is — the tour row answers it in the National Park Service's terms, "No. The National Park Service directs visitors along a paved, wheelchair-accessible 0.3-mile trail to view the cliff dwelling from its base; visitors do not enter the dwelling. Check current monument access before the visit." — so the day is built around viewing and walking rather than around a tour nobody sells. The published window is 6-7 hours and it bills 6 hours, so the day starts at $750 and the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $870 before 8% tax. Reservations: (623) 986-6339.

Last updated: September 18, 2026

Can you go inside the cliff dwelling at Montezuma Castle?

No. The tour's own answer puts it in the National Park Service's words — "The National Park Service directs visitors along a paved, wheelchair-accessible 0.3-mile trail to view the cliff dwelling from its base; visitors do not enter the dwelling" — and that single fact shapes the whole 7-hour day priced below. The National Park Service gives the reason in its own words: "Even though they might not look like it, Montezuma Castle and the other dwellings are fragile and very sensitive to human activity." The same page asks every visitor to "stay on the marked trails and do not climb walls." What that leaves is better than it sounds. The dwelling is viewed from below, on the ground, at whatever pace a group sets — which is exactly the kind of stop a private vehicle suits, because nothing about the visit is timed by somebody else's departure.

What is a private Montezuma Castle tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale?

It is the whole vehicle and one chauffeur held for a 7-hour day to the monument and back, not a seat on somebody else's coach. 6 vehicles are offered for it, from 6 to 29 seats, and priced from $750 to $1,770, every figure quoted in writing first. Scottsdale Sprinters sells the transport around the stops you confirm, never the monument visit itself. Your group decides who is aboard and how the hours are spent; the chauffeur drives, parks, waits while you are on the trail, and drives home. The row publishes the day as 6-7 hours, and the whole booking is that window with the vehicle waiting between the two trailheads. Per head the arithmetic is plainer than it looks. The 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter splits $870 across its seats, about $62 each; the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) splits $1,350 across 29, about $47. Those are the current published hourly rates carried across this day, never a fare per person, and monument admission is separate.

How does the day run, from the Camp Verde stop to the return?

The tour publishes 9 steps and states the day as 6-7 hours. Two of them are conditional in the row's own wording — the second monument and the last stop — so a group that wants a slower morning simply spends more of the window on step 3. "Drive to the confirmed Camp Verde-area stop" is the fixed point, and "Morning pickup" is set backward from it. "Continue to Montezuma Well if current access and timing permit" is written as a condition rather than a promise, and the final stop is published as optional, so neither is something this page will pretend to guarantee. The row also publishes what the day is meant to show: Montezuma Castle National Monument, Montezuma Well, Monument history and archaeology, Montezuma Well landscape, Verde Valley scenery, Optional: Tuzigoot ruins. That list is the whole brief. Morning pickup Drive to the confirmed Camp Verde-area stop Montezuma Castle visitor center & viewing Paved 0.3-mile viewing trail to the base of the cliff dwelling Continue to Montezuma Well if current access and timing permit Well rim trail & ancient irrigation canals Lunch in Camp Verde or Cottonwood Optional: Tuzigoot National Monument Return to Scottsdale

Which vehicle fits the group, and what does the day cost?

Group size decides it. This tour offers 6 vehicles, and every row below prices the identical 7-hour day: the published hourly rate times 6 billable hours, because 7 requested hours earn 1 free hour on the standard ladder, against each vehicle's own 4-hour minimum. Up to 6 travellers the Luxury SUV (Suburban) runs the day for $750, which is where the row's own list starts with the Luxury SUV (Suburban); the Executive Black Sprinter and Executive White Sprinter share a rate at $145 an hour. Past 14 seats it is the Mini Bus (24 Pax) and the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). The per-seat column divides the day total by seated capacity — friends splitting one fare. The Luxury SUV (Suburban) is the least expensive day at $750; the Mini Bus (24 Pax) the least expensive seat at $46. The whole vehicle starts at $750 for the window the row publishes. What is in the fare, and what is not?

A 7-hour day in the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $870 before 8% tax — $145 an hour across 6 billable hours, roughly $62 a seat split 14 ways. The least expensive vehicle on the list runs the same day for $750. Three rules build every number: the day is priced by the hour against each vehicle's published minimum, hours above the ladder's rungs earn free hours, and 8% tax is the only addition. Nothing is by the mile or per passenger. 50% is taken today by card, the balance 48 hours before pickup. What the fare excludes is the part of the day that is not ours to sell: monument admission, and anything the park service charges or schedules. Lunch is a stop rather than a service for the same reason — "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop."

Is Montezuma Well part of the same monument, and is it always open?

It is part of the monument and it is somewhere else. The park service invites visitors to "Explore the geology, plants, and animals of Montezuma Well, a separate unit of Montezuma Castle National Monument", which is why the row makes it step 5 of 9 and makes it conditional. The row's wording is the honest one: "Continue to Montezuma Well if current access and timing permit". Access and timing are the park service's to publish and change, so the group confirms them and the vehicle is held for the window either way. On its own subject the row sends you to the same place: "Use the National Park Service's current monument information for the site's geology, history, trails, and access. The transportation request should include only the stops and timing the group has confirmed." What the park service says the place is stays stable enough to repeat: "Montezuma Well provided a stable source of water to the Sinagua." Step 6 of the itinerary — "Well rim trail & ancient irrigation canals" — is the part of the day that follows from that.

Does the day work for children, and how much walking is there?

Both answers belong to the monument rather than to us, and the row says so: "Review the monument's current family, trail, accessibility, and Junior Ranger information directly, then choose stops that fit the group." What this page can tell you is the vehicle's part — one cabin for 7 hours, with the walking confined to 2 short published stops. The itinerary states the first of them plainly: "Paved 0.3-mile viewing trail to the base of the cliff dwelling". That is the row's own figure and the park service's own trail; nothing here adds a gradient, a duration or a difficulty rating to it. Inside the vehicle the chauffeur is a resource rather than a fixture: "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really." Coats, bags and water stay aboard between stops, which on a monument day with two trailheads is what the vehicle is there for.

Where can the day start, and how is it quoted?

Pickup is a street address in any of the 10 metro cities with a published service-area page, not a zone or a depot. Reserving takes 3 things — the date, the number of people and one address — plus the stops your group has confirmed at the monument. The published service areas are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. One pickup address for the whole party keeps a group together, and this corridor's longer days — the wine country, the red rocks and the Jerome and Prescott run — are quoted the same way, each from its own published window. Every figure here is today's published table; the quote you act on is the written one, naming the vehicle, the hours, the 8% tax and the 50% deposit, confirmed before anything is charged. Call Scottsdale Sprinters on (623) 986-6339, or send those 3 things and request a current quote.
